newsitem.title: USA: LIPA plans to sell up to $7.3 billion of debt.
newsitem.headline: LIPA plans to sell up to $7.3 billion of debt.

text.p: Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) said Wednesday it plans to sell up to $7.3 billion of tax-free debt to pay for its purchase of assets owned by Brooklyn Union Gas and Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO).
Senior officials from LIPA and Bear, Stearns, which is serving as the financial adviser, told Reuters LIPA would sell $4.297 billion of tax-free bonds when the transaction closes.
LIPA is a state agency created in 1987 to resolve problems with the failed Shoreham nuclear power plant on Long Island.

The first debt sale would pay for $2.5 billion of common stock in a holding company being jointly established by Brooklyn Union and LILCO as part of their planned merger, said Bob Foran, senior managing director at Bear, Stearns.
He explained that the second sale of $1.424 billion of tax-free bonds, expected to occur within three months of the deal's closing, would be used partly to refinance high-coupon bonds.

Within six to 18 months after completion of the transaction, LIPA might sell another $1.541 billion of tax-free bonds, but only if market conditions are favorable, said Foran and LIPA trustee Patrick Foye.
LIPA officials, at a news conference Wednesday in Uniondale, N.Y., said they expected the deal with Brooklyn Union and LILCO to close in late 1997 or early 1998.
LIPA Chairman Frank Zarb said the financing plan includes having LILCO and Brooklyn Union buy an interest rate hedge, a provision he called "almost a deal breaker."
Zarb said he was confident the market could absorb what would be one of the country's largest ever series of tax-free bond sales.
"The market is big enough to take it. At any given time you have got to measure the receptivity of the market (but) the bankers are pretty comfortable with what we laid out before them," he said.
